evidence: coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:5703-5732 writes exactly four realtime frames and then withholds only the terminal; the realtime producer is finite rather than continuously ready.
coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:5737-5755 writes one PlayerState plus eight interactions and then stops; the control producer is also finite.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:5772-5775 waits for notification that bytes were written to the sockets, not that the coordinator and control pump futures are simultaneously ready at each scheduler poll.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:5783-5835 asserts only eventual counts. A scheduler that repeatedly chose control plus realtime while both were ready, then serviced heartbeat after either finite source drained, would still satisfy these assertions—the exact r2 starvation shape this test is intended to reject.
findings.impact: The r4 production scheduler is structurally round-robin, but a future regression to the previously confirmed multi-source starvation behavior could pass this required deterministic regression test.
findings.observation: The revised active_round_robin test still does not hold control, realtime, and due heartbeat simultaneously ready or assert their bounded selection order, so F-2FFF4874 is not resolved.
findings.recommendation: Test the arbitration helper with synchronized/mock readiness sources, or use explicit pump/coordinator readiness barriers plus sustained producers. Make all three branches ready before each of several polls and assert the exact C/R/H rotation (and terminal preemption) rather than eventual counts after finite queues drain.
